_comment: SYNTHETIC fixture. In a real run the model authors this from the crossed work list; it is fixed here so the deterministic chain can be regression tested. A representative subset, not the full set.

managed.statement: Every read of an order record must verify that the record belongs to the tenant of the authenticated caller before the record is returned.
managed.rationale: Authentication establishes who is calling, not what they may reach. Ownership is checked separately, in the data access path rather than the route handler, so that new endpoints inherit it.
managed.team_part: Enforce tenant scoping in the database through row-level security or per-tenant schemas.

verification.expect: tenant predicate present on every order query, or row-level security enabled on the table
verification.fallback_manual: Request an order belonging to another tenant with a valid session; expect 404.

managed.statement: Presigned export URLs must expire within 15 minutes of issue.
managed.rationale: A presigned URL is an unauthenticated access path that no bucket policy will reveal. Bounding its lifetime bounds the exposure once the link leaves the tenant.
managed.team_part: Bound the expiry argument at the signing call site.

verification.expect: expiry argument bounded at 900 seconds or less
verification.fallback_manual: Issue an export, then retry the URL after the stated window; expect denial.

managed.statement: Personal data must be removed from exception payloads before they are transmitted to the error reporting service.
managed.rationale: Derived from a threat with no matching baseline control. The error reporter is a third-party boundary crossing introduced by a library call, so it does not appear in the network topology an infrastructure review would examine.
managed.team_part: Register a scrubbing hook on the error client covering request body, headers, and user context.

verification.expect: a beforeSend hook that strips user context fields
verification.fallback_manual: Trigger a handled exception carrying a member email; inspect the delivered event.

managed.statement: Refund webhook processing must be idempotent on an identifier supplied by the payment provider rather than by the caller.
managed.rationale: Derived from a threat with no matching baseline control. Business logic abuse of this kind is invisible to both control catalogues and code scanners, because the replayed request is well formed.
managed.team_part: Persist the provider event identifier with a uniqueness constraint; reject duplicates before applying any ledger effect.

verification.expect: uniqueness constraint on the provider event id, checked before the ledger write
verification.fallback_manual: Replay a captured refund webhook; expect exactly one ledger entry.

managed.statement: Analytics identifiers held as anonymous must not be joinable to account records.
managed.rationale: Derived from a LINDDUN linkability threat. STRIDE does not model this class, so it does not surface from a standard threat model, nor from any control in the baseline.
managed.team_part: Rotate the device identifier on each session, or hold the mapping in a store that account services cannot reach.

verification.expect: no session identifier or account identifier emitted alongside device_id
verification.fallback_manual: Attempt to join the analytics table to the account table on any shared column.

managed.statement: The audit log destination must not be writable by any identity whose actions it records.
managed.rationale: An audit log an actor can alter is not audit evidence. The separation has to hold at the destination, because application-level restraint fails once code execution is obtained.
managed.team_part: Deliver audit records to a destination in a separate trust domain from the application execution role.
managed.evidence: AWS SOC 2 Type II report, plus the IAM policy attached to the runtime role

verification.target: IAM policy for the application execution role
verification.expect: no write or delete permission on the audit log destination
verification.fallback_manual: Attempt a delete against the log destination using the runtime role.

managed.statement: Database connections carrying personal data must use TLS 1.2 or higher with server certificate verification.
managed.rationale: The engine accepts unencrypted connections unless the parameter group refuses them, most drivers do not verify the certificate by default, so neither end enforces this without explicit configuration.
managed.csp_part: Provides the server certificate on the managed endpoint.
managed.team_part: Force TLS in the parameter group; enable certificate verification in the client driver.
managed.evidence: AWS SOC 2 Type II report, plus the parameter group configuration

verification.expect: rds.force_ssl = 1 for PostgreSQL, require_secure_transport = ON for MySQL
verification.fallback_manual: Attempt a plaintext connection from a permitted network location; expect refusal.

managed.statement: Personal data at rest must be encrypted with a customer-managed key.
managed.rationale: Provider-managed keys leave the organisation without key custody. For RDS the choice is irreversible in place, which is why it is settled at design time rather than found in review.
managed.csp_part: Operates the key management infrastructure and the encryption mechanism.
managed.team_part: Enable default encryption on each store; supply a customer-managed key.
managed.evidence: AWS SOC 2 Type II report, plus terraform state

verification.expect: sse_algorithm = aws:kms with a customer-managed key arn; storage_encrypted = true
verification.fallback_manual: Console > S3 > bucket > Properties > Default encryption.
